comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded computing portfolio and AI capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD leads in embedded computing with CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs, and Adaptive SoCs used in automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage, and networking markets, incorporating dedicated AI processing capabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose automotive technology offerings. QCOM lists 'automotive platform features such as digital cockpit and ADAS/AD' as part of its significant technologies, while AMD describes its embedded computing portfolio as being used in the 'automotive' market, incorporating 'dedicated AI processing capabilities' for these applications.

sentences.text: • automotive platform features such as digital cockpit and ADAS/AD, to enable in-cabin experiences and assisted driving solutions;

We are a leader in embedded computing, where we deliver high-performance and scalability across a full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs that are used in a variety of markets, including automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage and networking.
We also incorporate dedicated AI processing capabilities into our embedded portfolio.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS/GNSS solutions for mobile devices, including integrated combination chips and location platform services.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO disclose specific wireless connectivity technologies for mobile devices. QCOM highlights 'Smart Transmit technology' for optimizing data speeds and 'Bluetooth' as part of its broader technology portfolio, while AVGO explicitly lists 'discrete and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions' and 'combination chips' for smartphones and wearables. Both address the wireless connectivity layer for mobile/other industries.

sentences.text: • XR platform features such as 6DoF (six-degrees of freedom) head tracking and controller capabilities, video pass-through and embedded cellular connectivity for new types of user experiences, and hybrid computing to distribute workloads across devices;
• Qualcomm® Smart Transmit™ technology, a modem-to-antenna technology that optimizes data speeds while complying with RF transmit power limits; and

• Connectivity Solutions: Our connectivity solutions include discrete and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions, and global positioning system/global navigation satellite system ("GPS/GNSS") receivers, designed for use in mobile devices including smartphones, tablets and wearable products.
Bluetooth is a low power technology that enables direct connectivity between devices.

comparisons.peer_summary: NOR products are non-volatile, re-writable devices providing fast read speeds for code storage and small data storage in automotive, industrial, and consumer applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and MU identify the 'automotive' market as a key application for their respective semiconductor products. QCOM includes 'automotive platform features' in its technology overview, while MU specifies that its NOR memory products are 'ideal for automotive... applications' alongside industrial and consumer uses.

NOR is most commonly used for reliable code storage (e.g., boot, application, operating system, and execute-in-place code in an embedded system) and for frequently changing small data storage and is ideal for automotive, industrial, and consumer applications.

comparisons.peer_summary: Managed NAND combines NAND flash with controllers and firmware to handle wear leveling and error correction internally, used in eMMC and UFS for mobile, automotive, and industrial markets.

QCOM describes technologies used in 'Mobile and Other Industries' including 'automotive platform features', while MU's Managed NAND products (eMMC/UFS) are 'widely used across the mobile, automotive, and industrial markets'.
